children.label: Causes

children.label: Greed

children.label: False Philanthropy
children.description: The desire to do good to some by robbing others via law.

children.label: Law as Instrument of Plunder

children.label: Subsidies
children.description: Tax money given to favored groups.

children.label: Progressive Taxation
children.description: Using the tax code to redistribute.

children.label: Public Schools
children.description: Tax funded schooling used for indoctrination.

children.label: Government Jobs Programs
children.description: Make-work at taxpayer expense.

children.label: Minimum Wage Laws
children.description: Price floor on labor that creates unemployment.

children.label: Welfare
children.description: Organized transfer presented as the poor's right to plunder.

children.label: Usury Laws
children.description: Interest caps that reduce credit for the poor.

children.label: Monopolies
children.description: State-granted exclusive privileges.

children.label: Forced Labor
children.description: Compulsory service extracted by the state.

children.description: Tariff effects and political economy.

children.label: Effacing Justice
children.description: Law that sanctions plunder destroys the distinction between justice and injustice.

children.label: Politicization
children.description: When law = plunder, politics becomes the main arena of life.

children.label: Rent Seeking
children.description: Resources spent obtaining political transfers rather than producing value.

children.label: Corruption of Education
children.description: State-paid teachers will not criticize the laws that pay them.

children.label: Loss of Moral Sense
children.description: Citizens must choose between conscience and respect for law.

children.label: Class Conflict
children.description: Every group organizes to plunder or to defend against plunder.

children.label: Economic Impoverishment
children.description: Legal plunder reduces total wealth even for many of its beneficiaries.

children.label: Instability
children.description: Generalized plunder produces constant pressure for upheaval.

children.label: Demoralization
children.description: When law commands injustice citizens become cynics or accomplices.

children.label: Natural Law
children.description: Rights inhere in human nature; positive law is valid only insofar as it recognizes them.

children.label: Rule of Law
children.description: Law must be general and equal. Targeting specific groups for plunder violates the rule of law.

children.label: Individual Rights
children.description: The moral unit is the individual; collective force exists only to protect individuals.

children.label: Property Rights
children.description: Property is the extension of faculties. Attacks on property are attacks on liberty and personality.

children.label: Free Trade
children.description: Exchange is production. Barriers are plunder.

children.label: Voluntary Philanthropy
children.description: True giving requires a willing giver. Coercion destroys the moral act.

children.label: Spontaneous Order
children.description: When law stays within its sphere, order emerges naturally.

children.label: Limited vs Activist State
children.description: The activist state that tries to organize everything becomes the central plunderer.

nodes.title: Foreword by Thomas J. DiLorenzo
nodes.label: Foreword
nodes.description: Places the essay in the tradition of the Declaration of Independence and warns against modern forms of legal plunder.
nodes.body:
# Foreword

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
DiLorenzo emphasizes Bastiat's anticipation of rent-seeking and the corruption of education and charity by the state. America came closest to the ideal except for slavery and tariffs.

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Government's only legitimate end is protection of life, liberty, and property. (see Natural Rights).
- Legal plunder includes tariffs, subsidies, progressive taxes, public schooling, welfare. (see legal plunder).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md).

nodes.title: Collective Force

nodes.body:
# Collective Force

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
Individuals may combine their right of defense into a regular common force. See the [central definition](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md).

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- The common force inherits exactly the same moral limits as individual force.
- It cannot lawfully be used for plunder. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see legal plunder).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md).

nodes.title: Law as the Organization of Defense
nodes.label: Law Defined as Organized Defense
nodes.description: Law is the substitution of collective force for individual force for the sole purpose of protecting persons, liberties and property.
nodes.body:
# Law Defined

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
This is the central thesis. Law has no other legitimate mission. When it goes beyond defense it becomes plunder. This definition is referenced from almost every other concept in the bundle.

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Collective force may only do what the individual may lawfully do. (see Natural Rights).
- Results in minimal, just, stable government. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see Natural Rights).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md).

# Lawful Defense

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
Every person has a natural right to defend life, liberty and property. See the [central definition](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md).

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Defense is the origin of legitimate force. (see Natural Rights).
- Collective right derives directly from it. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see Natural Rights).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md).

nodes.title: Natural Rights
nodes.label: Natural Rights
nodes.description: Life, liberty and property are God-given and exist prior to any legislation.
nodes.body:
# Natural Rights

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
These three gifts precede and justify law. Any statute violating them is illegitimate. See how they ground the [definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md).

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Three elements: personality (individuality), liberty, property. (see Natural Rights).
- Legislation must serve them, not create or destroy them. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see Natural Rights).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [rent-seeking behavior](/legal-plunder/consequences/rent-seeking.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [modern examples](/modern-relevance/contemporary-plunder.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [false philanthropy](/perversion-of-law/false-philanthropy.md).

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).

- Foundation of limited government. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see Natural Rights).

# Order and Stability

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
A government that only protects produces the most stable and natural social order. See the [central definition](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md).

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- No artificial displacements of capital or population.
- Individuals bear responsibility for success and misfortune. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see Natural Rights).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md).

nodes.title: Legal Plunder
nodes.label: legal plunder
nodes.description: Law used to take the property of some and give it to others without consent.
nodes.body:
# Definition of Legal Plunder

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
The fatal principle that law may organize plunder. Once admitted, every class tries to capture the power to plunder. This page is one of the central hubs of the bundle.

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Plunder made respectable by law. (see legal plunder).
- Leads to universal plunder when the victims seize the legislature. The opposite occurs through the [causes of perversion](/perversion-of-law/causes-of-perversion.md). (see legal plunder).

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [rent-seeking behavior](/legal-plunder/consequences/rent-seeking.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [modern examples](/modern-relevance/contemporary-plunder.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [false philanthropy](/perversion-of-law/false-philanthropy.md).

Law diverted from protection to predation.

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Becomes the tool of avarice instead of its check.

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md).

nodes.title: The Law
nodes.label: The Law
nodes.description: Bastiat's treatise: law exists to protect natural rights; when turned into plunder it destroys justice and liberty.
nodes.body:
# The Law (1850)

These principles are developed in [The Law](/the-law.md) and rest on [Natural Rights](/fundamental-principles/natural-rights.md).
Bastiat shows that life, liberty and property precede legislation. The law (see [/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md)) is the organization of the natural right of defense. When perverted (by greed or false philanthropy) it becomes an engine of legal plunder. The remedy is to return law strictly to its defensive sphere. See also the detailed treatment of the [core definition](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md).

## Key Points

For the foundational treatment, see [the definition of law](/fundamental-principles/law-as-organization-of-defense.md) and [the proper sphere of law](/true-law/proper-sphere.md).
- Personality, liberty and property are natural and pre-political. (see Natural Rights).
- Law = collective force organized only for protection. (see Natural Rights).
- Perversion turns law into legalized theft benefiting some at expense of others.
- Consequences: moral confusion, politicized society, rent-seeking, impoverishment.

For more, see [legal plunder](/legal-plunder/definition.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [rent-seeking behavior](/legal-plunder/consequences/rent-seeking.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [modern examples](/modern-relevance/contemporary-plunder.md). Related consequences appear in the discussion of [false philanthropy](/perversion-of-law/false-philanthropy.md).
